Andhra Pradesh had more assets and hence more debt
Population ratio was the sole factor for distribution of debt
Union Government decided that Andhra Pradesh has to bear more debt
key_text: Population ratio was the sole factor for distribution of debt
explanation: Debt and most liabilities were apportioned by population ratio (58.32 : 41.68), so AP with the larger population took the larger share of debt; assets went by location.

exam: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
q: President Rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh in 1973 because of:
explanation: President's Rule (Jan–Dec 1973) was imposed because of the Jai Andhra agitation, after P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned.

notes.text: - **President's Rule: 18 Jan – 10 Dec 1973** (~11 months) – the **first** in Andhra Pradesh and the **longest**; imposed because of the Jai Andhra agitation.

exam: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
q: The Jai Andhra Movement 1972-73 finally ended with
options: The arrest of many students and women leaders
The suppression by central reserved forces
The Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
key_text: The Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
explanation: Jai Andhra ended with the Centre's Six-Point Formula (1973); the agitation was called off on 1 October 1973. It was not ended by repression or arrests.

notes.text: - **Ended by the Six-Point Formula** (21 Sep 1973); agitation called off **1 Oct 1973** – not by repression, arrests or mere Mulki abolition.

Imposition of high taxes on Andhras
